entries.title: Choose whether abstains count as completed reviews
entries.summary: A new **Reviews** section in Program settings holds settings for every review plan and round in the event. Its first setting, **Count abstains as completed reviews**, is on by default, so nothing changes until you turn it off. Off, an abstain is left out of progress, review counts and reports: a submission with two scores and one abstain shows 2 reviews, and a reviewer who reviews 9 and abstains on 1 shows 9 of 9. Abstains are still listed as abstains.

enable.path: On by default. To stop counting abstains: Program → Settings → Reviews → turn off Count abstains as completed reviews

entries.use_case: A committee that wants every submission to get three real scores turns this off, so an abstain no longer makes a submission look fully reviewed and they can see where to assign another reviewer.

cs_action.note: On by default, so counts are unchanged. A customer who wants abstains left out of review counts switches off Count abstains as completed reviews under Program → Settings → Reviews.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An admin says review totals or progress look too high because abstains are counted, or a minimum-reviews check passes on abstains.

entries.title: Awards checkout hides the promo code box when there are no codes
entries.summary: When an awards program has no active promo code, the submission checkout no longer shows the **Promo code** field and **Apply** button. Applicants aren't left wondering about a discount they were never given. The box comes back as soon as you add an active code. Pricing and payment are unchanged.

where.path: Awards Site → submission → Complete Your Payment

entries.use_case: An awards program that doesn't use promo codes gets a cleaner checkout: applicants see the fee and the Pay button, with no empty promo code field.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Programs with an active promo code look the same as before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to hide the promo code field, or applicants ask support for a promo code.

entries.title: Long SSO names fit the Site sign-in button
entries.summary: The **Sign in with …** SSO button on Site sign-in pages now grows and wraps onto a second line when the SSO name is long, so the full label and its icon stay inside the button and the sign-in card. Short names look the same as before.

where.path: Site sign-in card → Sign in with <SSO name>

entries.use_case: Organizations whose SSO provider has a long display name, such as "America's Credit Unions Account", get a sign-in button that reads cleanly on desktop and phones.

cs_action.note: Automatic for every Site with SSO.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports the SSO button text spilling out of the sign-in card.

entries.title: Move a signed-in reviewer's role to a new email address
entries.summary: Admins can now change the email on a reviewer who has already signed in or scored. Typing a new address in the edit dialog opens a **Review the move** panel that shows how many rounds and saved reviews will transfer and whether the new address already has an account. **Move to new@…** confirms the transfer; the reviewer's original sign-in is unaffected. If the new address already reviews the same rounds, a conflict message explains what must be resolved first. Applies to the Review Plan 2.0 reviewers list, the interest-form evaluators tab, and the Awards **Edit Reviewer** modal.

where.path: Review Plans → [Plan] → Reviewers → Edit reviewer  |  Awards → [Program] → Reviewers → Edit Reviewer

entries.use_case: When a reviewer changes jobs or submits under the wrong email, an admin can move their reviewer role — including all round assignments and saved scores — to the correct address without touching the reviewer's sign-in credentials or other roles.

cs_action.note: Default on; no setup required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports being unable to update a reviewer's email after that reviewer has signed in or submitted scores.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running Review Plan 2.0 or Awards with reviewers who have already signed in.
internal.staff_path: Review Plans → [Plan] → Reviewers → click a reviewer → email field
internal.gotchas: If the target address already reviews the same rounds, the move is blocked until one reviewer is removed from the shared rounds. The reviewer's original sign-in account and any other roles it holds are never changed.
internal.talk_track: If a reviewer signed in under the wrong email, you can now move their role and all their scores to the right address — the old sign-in keeps working for everything else.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the email-reassign flow: the Review the move panel, what the dry-run preview shows (rounds, saved reviews, account status), the conflict state, and the fact that the reviewer's original sign-in is unchanged.
draft.why_use_it: Review plans accumulate scores and assignments tied to a specific email address. When that address needs to change — because a reviewer switched employers, used a personal address by mistake, or merged accounts — the reassign flow moves the reviewer role and all its history to the new address in one step, shows a preview of what will transfer, and flags any conflicts before anything is changed.

entries.title: Change a signed-in reviewer's email by moving their role to the new address
entries.summary: Admins can now update the email address of a reviewer who has already signed in, saved scores, or belongs to another organisation. Instead of editing the sign-in account (which is blocked), the reviewer's role, roster entry, assignments, **saved scores**, plan enrolment, tags, categories, recommendations, alternates and Session Build data move to the account that owns the new address — creating one if none exists. A **dry run** option shows what would move and how many scores are affected before any change is written. If the target account already reviews any of the same rounds or items, the request is blocked with a clear conflict message.

where.path: Review Plans → Reviewers → (reviewer row) → Edit email

entries.use_case: A reviewer submitted abstracts under one email and was also added as a reviewer — so they had already signed in and saved scores. The admin can now correct the reviewer's email without losing any of their scores or assignments; everything moves to the new address automatically.

cs_action.note: Default on; no setup required. The existing resend-invite action sends the new account its invitation.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports they cannot change a reviewer's email because the person has already signed in or saved scores.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running Review Plan 2.0, Awards review rounds, or interest-form evaluation plans where a reviewer used the wrong email address.
internal.staff_path: Review Plans → Reviewers → edit a reviewer's email
internal.gotchas: No invite email is sent automatically to a newly created account — the admin must use the existing resend-invite action. The org contact record is not relinked to the new account. A 409 conflict is returned if the target account already reviews any of the same rounds or items, or if the address belongs to a deleted account.
internal.talk_track: If a reviewer signed in under the wrong email and already saved scores, you can now move their entire reviewer role — scores, assignments, recommendations and all — to the correct address in one step, with a dry-run preview before anything changes.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the role-move email-change flow for signed-in reviewers, including the dry-run option, what data moves, conflict conditions (409), and the need to manually resend the invite to a newly created account.
draft.why_use_it: Review plans let you score and rank submissions before accepting them. Reviewers sign in with a single account that spans every organisation, so their email address cannot simply be overwritten once they have used it. The role-move approach lets admins correct a reviewer's address at any time — even after scores are saved — while keeping the old account's sign-in, other events and submitter role completely intact.

entries.title: Send attendee Advocacy embed setup to your web team by email
entries.summary: On the **Share** tab of an attendee Advocacy campaign, use **Send to your web team** to email up to 10 addresses at once. Each recipient gets a private link to a read-only setup page showing the campaign details, embed source and any note you added — no Sessionboard seat required. Links can be revoked from the same tab, and the log shows who was sent each link and when.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → [Attendees campaign] → Share tab → Send to your web team

entries.use_case: Vendors and web teams who paste Advocacy embeds often don't have a Sessionboard login, and copying embed code into Gmail rewrites every URL. Send each person their own private setup link so they can view the embed details in a browser without needing an account or receiving broken code in email.

cs_action.note: Default on; no flag or env var required. Deploy web-api before the matching UI PR ships or the Share tab card will 404.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer mentions sending embed code to a registration vendor, AV team or web agency who does not have a Sessionboard seat.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running an attendee Advocacy campaign who hands off embed setup to an outside party.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → [Attendees campaign] → Share tab
internal.gotchas: The UI PR must ship after this API PR; if the UI ships first the Share tab card returns 404. Only Attendees campaign types support setup shares — speaker and exhibitor campaigns do not. Limit is 10 addresses per send, 20 sends per minute.
internal.talk_track: Instead of pasting embed code into an email where every link gets rewritten, you send your vendor a private link to a setup page. They open it in a browser, see the campaign details and embed source, and you can revoke the link any time.

draft.docs_gap: The advocacy-attendees guide should add a section explaining how to use Send to your web team: how to enter addresses and an optional note, what the recipient sees on the setup page, and how to view the send log and revoke a link.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy for attendees lets you put a personalised sharing card on your registration confirmation page or in your emails so every attendee can promote the event to their network. Sending the embed setup to an outside vendor or web team is a common step, and the setup share keeps that handoff clean: each recipient gets a direct link to a read-only page with everything they need, and you can revoke access at any time from the Share tab.

entries.title: Sessionboard Awards is now available as a self-serve product
entries.summary: A dedicated Awards workspace at `/awards/:orgId` lets organizers sign up for Sessionboard Awards directly, without going through the platform. The workspace includes **Home**, **Programs**, nominations, reviews, **Winners**, **Results**, **Apps** (AI assistants and Public API), and **Billing**. Features requiring an Enterprise plan — a second review round, entry fees and payments, SSO, and a named CSM — appear as locked **Enterprise** items that open the upgrade page.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Awards

entries.use_case: An association or media company that runs annual awards programs can now sign up for Sessionboard Awards on their own, set up nomination programs, manage reviewers, and pick winners — all without a sales conversation. Teams that need a second review round, entry fees, or SSO can upgrade to Enterprise directly from the locked items in the workspace.

cs_action.note: Sign-up is behind the AWARDS_SIGNUP_ENABLED flag and Stripe sandbox products (awd_* lookup keys) plus the Awards billing portal config are not yet created — Checkout must be set up before the self-serve flow is live in production. Do not promote to customers until the web-api Awards routes ship.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or customer asks about running an awards or recognition program independently, or when an existing Awards (platform) customer asks about a lighter self-serve option.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organization that runs annual awards, recognition programs, or CFP-style competitions and wants to get started without a platform contract.
internal.staff_path: /awards/:orgId — Home, Programs, Reviews, Winners, Results, Apps, Billing
internal.gotchas: Sign-up is gated by AWARDS_SIGNUP_ENABLED env flag. Stripe products for Awards billing are not yet created, so Checkout will fail until those are provisioned. The nomination form is not yet editable (stubbed). There is no public vote or winners showcase page yet. The People page reuses Marketing's page. Platform /org and /event Awards screens are unchanged.
internal.talk_track: You can now sign up for Sessionboard Awards directly and run your entire program — nominations, reviews, winners — from a dedicated workspace. If you need a second review round, entry fees, or SSO, those are one upgrade away.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guide should document the self-serve sign-up flow at /signup/awards, the workspace navigation (Home, Programs, Reviews, Winners, Results, Apps, Billing), and which features are locked to Enterprise plans (second review round, entry fees/payments, SSO, named CSM).
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Awards gives you a dedicated workspace to run the full lifecycle of an awards program: build nomination forms, open submissions, assign reviewers, score entries, and announce winners. It sits alongside Marketing and Learning in the same workspace frame, so your team works in one place whether they are promoting an event, running a course, or managing an awards cycle. Enterprise plans unlock a second review round, entry fees and payments, and SSO for larger programs.

entries.title: Query which Sessionboard products an org owns via the public API
entries.summary: Two new read-only endpoints — `GET /v1/products` and `GET /v1/organization/:orgId/products` — return the list of Sessionboard apps the organization owns, including each app's `key`, `owned` flag, how it was acquired (`via`), days remaining (`days_left`), and a `platform_customer` boolean. Any API token that carries at least one `read:*` scope can call these endpoints.
entries.use_case: Developers building integrations or AI assistants on top of Sessionboard can call this endpoint to discover which products an org has licensed — for example, to decide whether to surface Marketing or Awards features — without needing a separate out-of-band check.

cs_action.note: Endpoints are default-on for any token with a read scope. No setup required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or partner is building an integration or MCP-based AI assistant and needs to branch logic based on which Sessionboard products the org owns.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers or partners with API access who are building integrations, MCP servers, or AI assistants against the Sessionboard public API.
internal.gotchas: A token with only write scopes receives 403 SCOPE_REQUIRED. Legacy tokens with no scopes pass, consistent with existing API behaviour. The endpoint is scoped to the org from the token; passing another org's :orgId is refused.
internal.talk_track: If you're building an integration that needs to know whether a customer has Marketing, Awards or another add-on, the new /v1/products endpoint gives you that in one call — no heuristics needed.

draft.docs_gap: The API changelog and reference should document the request/response shape for GET /v1/products and GET /v1/organization/:orgId/products, including the fields key, owned, via, days_left and platform_customer, plus the scope requirements.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard public API lets you read and write event data programmatically. Knowing which products an organization owns lets your integration or AI assistant tailor its behaviour — showing only the tools the org has access to and skipping calls that would return 404 or 403 for unlicensed products.

entries.title: Write attendee registration and check-in states back to HubSpot Marketing Events
entries.summary: When the **HubSpot Attendance write-back** toggle is on, Sessionboard automatically pushes each attendee's state — **Registered**, **Attended** or **Cancelled** — to a matching HubSpot Marketing Event, once per day. Only attendees synced from a third-party registration provider (Cvent, Swapcard, Swoogo, etc.) are sent; Sessionboard-native and CSV-imported registrations are excluded. The toggle is off by default and must be enabled on the HubSpot connection.

enable.path: Organization Settings → Integrations → HubSpot → Write-back → Attendance (toggle on)

entries.use_case: An association that uses Cvent for registration and HubSpot for marketing wants every confirmed, checked-in or cancelled attendee reflected in HubSpot Marketing Events automatically, so post-event nurture sequences and engagement scoring stay accurate without a manual export.

cs_action.note: The attendance toggle is off by default. An admin must turn it on in the HubSpot connection settings. The UI toggle (in the write-back panel) ships in a separate web-ui-v2 PR; confirm that PR is merged before enabling for customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses HubSpot for marketing automation and a third-party registration platform (Cvent, Swapcard, Swoogo, etc.) and wants post-event nurture or lead scoring to reflect actual attendance.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with an active HubSpot OAuth connection, Pathways processing enabled, and attendees synced via the Attendees layer from a supported registration provider.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Integrations → HubSpot → Write-back → Attendance
internal.gotchas: Only attendees whose source is a third-party registration provider are sent — Sessionboard-native registrations and CSV imports are never written. The HubSpot connection must have the crm.objects.marketing_events.write scope; without it the run is refused. Suppressed contacts, withdrawn-consent records, anonymised registrations and merged duplicates are excluded. At most 10,000 attendance rows go per daily run; the rest carry over. The UI toggle is in a separate PR (web-ui-v2) — do not promise the setting is visible until that PR ships.
internal.talk_track: Once you turn on the attendance write-back, every confirmed, checked-in or cancelled attendee from your registration platform shows up in HubSpot Marketing Events automatically each day — no exports needed. Your nurture sequences and engagement scores stay current without any manual work.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide (or a dedicated HubSpot write-back guide) should document the Attendance write-back kind: how to enable it, which registration sources are included and excluded, the HubSpot Marketing Events API states that map to each attendee status, the daily run cadence, and the required HubSpot OAuth scope.
draft.why_use_it: The HubSpot write-back keeps your HubSpot Marketing Events in sync with what actually happened at your event. Confirmed registrations, check-ins and cancellations flow from your registration provider into HubSpot contacts automatically each day, so your marketing team's nurture sequences, lead scores and event-engagement reports reflect real attendance data without any manual exports or data wrangling.

entries.title: Site sign-in page no longer shows a false "You are offline" banner
entries.summary: The **"You are offline. Please check your internet connection."** banner and dimmed page on Sites no longer appear when the network is actually working. The overlay now confirms connectivity with a real HTTP probe before showing the bar, so VPN adapters, sleep/wake cycles, and browser DevTools throttle settings no longer trigger a false alarm.
entries.use_case: Attendees and speakers on VPNs or laptops that just woke from sleep were seeing a dimmed, unusable sign-in page even though the network was fine. This fix means the banner only appears when requests actually fail, so those users can sign in without confusion or a page refresh.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that portal or site visitors see an offline banner despite having a working internet connection.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose attendees or speakers use VPNs, corporate networks, or laptops that frequently sleep.
internal.gotchas: The banner still appears correctly when the network genuinely fails — it now uses a HEAD probe to /favicon.png with a 4-second timeout to verify before showing.
internal.talk_track: The offline warning now double-checks with a real network request before it shows, so VPN users and anyone on a laptop that just woke up won't see a false alarm on the sign-in page.

draft.docs_gap: The site-builder guide should note that the offline banner only appears when requests genuinely fail, not when the browser's network adapter reports disconnected.

entries.title: Submission forms: see who viewed a form and has not submitted
entries.summary: Each submission form card under **Program → Forms** now shows **N viewed**: the signed-in people who opened the form. It opens a list with each person's status (viewed only, draft started, submitted), first and last visit and number of visits. Filter to **Viewed, not submitted**, search, sort, export the rows as CSV, or email them in one step with the same email as **Email draft holders**. Visitors who were not signed in are not recorded, and your event team is left out of the count.

enable.path: Program → Forms → a form's card → N viewed

where.path: Program → Forms → a form's card → N viewed (or ⋯ → Who viewed)

entries.use_case: The organizer wants to follow up with everyone who looked at the call for papers but never submitted, including people who never started a draft.

cs_action.note: On for every event once released. Counting starts on release day in each region; nothing is backfilled.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how many people looked at their CFP, or wants to chase people who did not submit (Community idea "Form Visit Data", 4 orgs).
internal.who_should_get_it: Every org running a call for papers, especially with a close date coming up.
internal.staff_path: Program → Forms → a form's card → N viewed
internal.gotchas: Signed-in visitors only; anonymous opens are not recorded. Org members and event staff roles are excluded from the count and hidden by default; reviewers and portal users are counted. A refresh within 30 minutes is not a new visit. Email goes to the rows shown and shares the draft-holders 10-minute cooldown pattern on its own clock. Each new visit also writes a form.viewed signal (Pathways / engagement).
internal.talk_track: You can now see who opened your call for papers and never submitted, and email them from the same screen.

entries.title: Merge tags for subsessions and their parent session
entries.summary: Emails about sessions can now name an abstract and the session it belongs to: `{{{subsession_title}}}`, its ID, start, end, room and speakers, the matching `{{{parent_session_title}}}` tags, and `{{{my_subsessions_summary}}}`, a table of the recipient's subsessions. An email about a subsession shows that subsession. An email about a top-level session lists each recipient's own subsessions under it, by start time. Times use the event's timezone.

where.path: Sessions → Send → Merge Tags, Email Campaigns (Sessions audience) and Sessions email templates

entries.use_case: A medical meeting can send each presenting author "Your abstract {{{subsession_title}}} has been accepted for {{{parent_session_title}}}" with its time in the event's timezone, abstract by abstract, without telling the other abstracts in the session.

cs_action.note: Available in every event's merge tag picker for Sessions emails. To email one abstract at a time, send from Sessions with Sessions to include set to Subsessions only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with abstracts or posters as subsessions wants acceptance or scheduling emails that name the abstract and its session.

entries.title: The agenda calendar sticks to your event's days
entries.summary: **Day**, **Week**, **Month** and **Rooms** on the Agenda now show only the event's days, counted in the event time zone. Week is exactly the event's days, the arrows stop at the first and last day, and Month greys out the rest. **Event days only** turns it off, and a bar counts any scheduled session outside the event dates with **Show all dates**. When you schedule by hand, **Day** lists the event's days first (with **Another date…** for anything else), and the **Starts At** / **Ends At** pickers open on the event's month with its days marked.

where.path: Program → Agenda → Day / Week / Month / Rooms

entries.use_case: Building a three-day program no longer means paging past empty weeks: the calendar opens on the event's days and only moves between them.

cs_action.note: Automatic for events with dates. Admins who want the old view click Event days only to turn it off (remembered per event, per browser).

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to hide days outside the event on the agenda, or a session seems to be missing from the calendar (it may be on a day outside the event dates).

entries.title: Find contacts whose sessions were all declined
entries.summary: Contacts views have three new filters: **[Subsession] Status - All declined**, **[Session] Status - All declined** and **[Speaker] Status - All declined**. Each is checked only when every one of the contact's subsessions, sessions or speaker seats is declined. Reports can ask the same with `ALL`, `ANY` and `NONE`.

where.path: CRM → Speakers (or All Contacts) → Filter → Add Filter → [Subsession] Status - All declined

entries.use_case: Send a decline email once, only to people whose sessions (or, on events with subsessions, whose subsessions) were all declined. The subsession filter does not look at standalone sessions, so check those separately on an event that has both. The Session - Declined tab includes anyone with at least one declined session, even if another of their sessions was accepted.

cs_action.note: Automatic. The existing Session - Declined tab and [Session] Status - Declined filter still mean at least one declined session.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is preparing decline emails, or asks why someone with an accepted session shows on the Session - Declined tab.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with subsessions or speakers on several sessions, where a person can be declined on one and accepted on another.
internal.staff_path: CRM → Speakers → Filter → Add Filter → [Subsession] Status - All declined (events with subsessions) or [Session] Status - All declined (events without) → Is checked → Save as new view.
internal.gotchas: Every role counts: someone declined as a speaker but accepted as a moderator is not All declined. On events with subsessions use the [Subsession] filter; speakers also sit on the parent session, whose status is not a decision about them, so [Session] Status - All declined counts only parent sessions.
internal.talk_track: On an event without subsessions, filter on [Session] Status - All declined. On an event with subsessions, filter on [Subsession] Status - All declined, and if it also has standalone sessions, check those people's standalone sessions before sending, because the subsession filter does not look at them. Save it as a view, then select all and send the email with contact merge tags.

entries.title: Watch integration syncs in real time with a live progress log
entries.summary: While an event integration sync is running, a live log now streams step-by-step progress in **History → Integrations → Running**. Each phase — connecting to the vendor, reading sessions, syncing each entity type, retries, and the final outcome — appears as it happens, with counts of records created, updated, unchanged, and failed. Supported vendors: Swapcard, ExpoPlatform, Stova, Grip, Bizzabo, Gleanin, Cvent, Swoogo, and ASP. Speaker-only syncs and organization-level syncs don't show live lines yet, so an empty log for one of those jobs doesn't mean it failed.
entries.use_case: Organizers running a sync against a large vendor no longer have to wait until it finishes to know whether it is working. They can open the Running tab and watch each phase complete in real time, spot a rate-limit retry or a failed entity immediately, and decide whether to let the sync continue or investigate before it ends.

cs_action.note: Requires IS_ELASTICSEARCH_ENABLED on the environment. Confirm it is active before pointing customers to the Running tab. Only event syncs are covered in this release; speaker-only and org-level jobs do not emit lines yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why a sync is taking a long time, reports unexpected sync results, or wants more visibility into what a vendor integration is doing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Swapcard, ExpoPlatform, Stova, Grip, Bizzabo, Gleanin, Cvent, Swoogo, or ASP event syncs.
internal.staff_path: History → Integrations → Running
internal.gotchas: Speaker-only syncs (Swoogo, Cvent, Expo, Swapcard), org-level syncs, and inbound wrappers do not emit live lines yet. Mapper warnings stay in the system log only. Each vendor needs a manual sync to confirm its lines appear correctly — not yet validated against real vendors.
internal.talk_track: You can now watch your integration sync progress in real time — each phase, retry, and entity count appears as it happens, so you know immediately if the vendor is rate-limiting or if records are failing.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section describing the Running tab and how to read the live log lines, including what each phase label means, how retry messages appear, and what the terminal outcome statuses (completed, with warnings, with errors, failed) indicate.
draft.why_use_it: Integration syncs can take several minutes and touch thousands of records across speakers, sessions, rooms, and tracks. The live progress log lets you follow each phase as it runs — connecting, reading, syncing each entity type, handling retries — so you always know where a sync stands and what it produced. When something goes wrong, the log tells you whether the vendor is rate-limiting requests, returning errors, or failing on specific records, giving you the context to act without waiting for the sync to finish.

entries.title: Contact, group and account profile dropdowns now close when you click outside them
entries.summary: In the **Contact Profile**, **Group Profile** and **Account Profile** side panels, opening a dropdown or multi-select attribute field and then clicking elsewhere in the panel now closes the list. Previously, lists stayed open and stacked on top of each other when a second field was opened, covering the fields below.

where.path: Speakers → All Speakers → [contact] → Attributes; CRM → Contacts → [contact] → Attributes; CRM → Groups → [group] → Attributes; CRM → Accounts → [account] → Attributes

entries.use_case: Organizers editing attribute fields on a speaker, group or account profile can now open one dropdown, pick a value, and move to the next field without lists piling up and obscuring the panel.

cs_action.note: Automatic fix; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that dropdown or multi-select attribute fields in a speaker, group or account side panel stay open or stack on top of each other.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers using attribute fields on contact, group or account profiles.
internal.staff_path: Speakers → All Speakers → any contact → Attributes; org CRM → Contacts / Groups / Accounts → any record → Attributes
internal.gotchas: The fix removes a stopPropagation guard from three panels. Session profile dropdowns were already working correctly and are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: Editing attributes in a contact or account profile is now much smoother — open a field, pick a value, and the list closes cleanly so you can move to the next one.

draft.docs_gap: The contact profile guide should note that clicking outside an open attribute dropdown or multi-select closes it, and that only one list is open at a time.

entries.title: Contact merges now re-sync portal assignments for the surviving contact
entries.summary: When two contacts are merged, the surviving contact's portal membership is now automatically re-evaluated across every event they belong to — including events inherited from the removed duplicates. Previously, a merge with no carried field values skipped the portal sync, leaving the survivor on the wrong portal (for example, landing on the Default People Portal instead of a Submission Portal).
entries.use_case: An organizer who merges a submitter with a duplicate contact can trust that the survivor lands on the correct filtered portal (such as a Submission Portal) immediately after the merge, without needing to manually trigger a resync or edit the contact record.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic for all new merges. For the one known affected contact in event 6153, run Portals → ⋮ → Resync Portal Assignments, or make any edit to the contact to queue a sync.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that a merged contact is on the wrong portal or is missing from a filtered portal (e.g. Submission Portal) after a merge.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who uses filtered portals (e.g. is-submitter portals) and regularly merges duplicate contacts.
internal.staff_path: Portals → ⋮ → Resync Portal Assignments (POST /event/{id}/portals/resync) for any event where a pre-fix merge left a survivor on the wrong portal.
internal.gotchas: The fix applies only to merges performed after this deploy. Pre-existing stale memberships from past merges are not automatically corrected — a manual resync or contact edit is needed per event. US had 1 confirmed wrong-portal case; broader stale counts (929 contact-event pairs US, 323 EU) are mostly likely still correct since their filters may not depend on what the merge moved.
internal.talk_track: After a contact merge, the survivor is now automatically placed on the right portal based on their updated data — no manual resync needed.

draft.docs_gap: The merge guide should note that portal assignments are automatically re-synced for the surviving contact after a merge, including for events inherited from removed duplicates.

entries.title: Watch an integration sync in real time from History → Integrations
entries.summary: A new **Running** sub-tab in **History → Integrations** shows every sync still in progress and recently finished syncs that have logs. Opening a running sync shows its full lifecycle (**Queued → Provisioning → Running → Finalizing**), a record count, a job/sync ID card, and a live log console with level filters, search, auto-scroll, copy and download. After starting a manual sync, the toast now includes a **View progress** link that opens the running view in a new tab; the completion toast links to **View results**. The tab and toast links are currently visible to staff only; for all other users the tab appears with a lock icon and a "Coming soon" tooltip.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable access; then History → Integrations → Running

entries.use_case: When a large session or contacts sync is running, an organizer can open the Running tab to watch records process in real time and read the log — no more waiting until the sync finishes to find out whether something went wrong.

cs_action.note: The Running tab and toast links are behind the super-user flag. Non-staff users see a locked tab with a 'Coming soon' tooltip. The API side (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5327) must be deployed first. Coordinate deploy order before enabling for any customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why a sync is taking a long time, or when they want more visibility into what an integration is doing during a sync.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who run frequent or large integration syncs (sessions, contacts, Gleanin) and want real-time feedback.
internal.staff_path: History → Integrations → Running (super-user flag required)
internal.gotchas: The API endpoints must be live before the UI is enabled for any user. Non-staff users land on Sync History if they follow a ?job= or ?sync= link.
internal.talk_track: You can now watch a sync as it runs — see each lifecycle stage, how many records have been processed, and a live log you can filter, search, copy or download. When you kick off a manual sync, the toast gives you a direct link to that job's progress view.

draft.docs_gap: The /communications/email-sms-history guide should add a section documenting the Running sub-tab, the sync lifecycle stages, the log console controls (filters, search, auto-scroll, copy, download), and the toast links that appear after a manual sync.
draft.why_use_it: The Integrations history lets you see every sync that has run for an event, including its outcome, the records it touched, and a full log of what happened. Use it to confirm a sync completed cleanly, diagnose a mapping problem, or share a log with your integration partner when troubleshooting. The Running view extends this to syncs still in progress, so you can catch issues as they happen rather than after the fact.

entries.title: Show speakers with job title and company on agenda calendar cards
entries.summary: **Card Display** in the agenda calendar has a new option, **Participants by role**. Each session card lists its people grouped by role in the session's participant order, with their job title, company (or the affiliation chosen for that session) and salutation and honorific, each one a checkbox. Hover over a card, or tab to it, for the full list. Calendar card details now also open from the keyboard. Nothing changes until you add it.

enable.path: Program → Agenda → Card Display → Additional Fields → Participants by role

where.path: Program → Agenda → Day, Week, Month or Rooms → Card Display

entries.use_case: A program team building the schedule can see who is speaking in every slot, with their title and organization, without opening each session.

cs_action.note: Per user and per browser: each admin adds Participants by role under Card Display themselves.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to see speakers, faculty or their organizations on the agenda builder's calendar.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program teams scheduling large agendas, especially medical and scientific meetings that track faculty affiliations per session.
internal.staff_path: Program → Agenda → Week → Card Display (column icon above the Sessions panel) → Add a field → Participants by role
internal.gotchas: Company shows the session's own affiliations when the session has them. Cards are one line, so long lists are cut short; the hover or focus detail shows up to 12 people. Unscheduled cards in the side panel don't show participants.

entries.title: Embeds: choose which roles to show, now in feeds too
entries.summary: Every embed's **Roles to show** setting decides which participants appear: untick **Moderators** and **Chairpersons** to list speakers only on the Agenda, Sessions list, Schedule Itinerary and speaker widgets. JSON, XML, plain text and iCal feeds now follow it too, with the checkboxes under **Field Options**. On a Site, a session's page follows the customized Agenda page's roles. Existing embeds and feeds keep showing speakers, chairpersons and moderators until you change it.

enable.path: Publish → Embeds → an embed → Style Options → Participant Roles → Roles to show

where.path: Publish → Embeds → an embed → Style Options (feeds: Field Options) → Roles to show

entries.use_case: The organizer wants the public agenda or a website feed to list only speakers, without moderators or chairpersons.

cs_action.note: Nothing changes until an admin unticks a role. HTML embeds have had the setting since SB-8853; this adds feeds and Site session pages.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to hide moderators or chairpersons (Community idea "[Embeds] Hide Moderator + Chairperson", 2 orgs) or to show only one custom role in an embed or feed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs that publish an agenda embed, a JSON/XML/iCal feed or a Site agenda and use moderators, chairpersons or custom roles.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Embeds → an embed → Style Options → Participant Roles
internal.gotchas: Hidden roles are removed server-side, so they're not in the page source either. Refresh the embed cache to see a change before the 60-minute refresh. The control needs Session Settings or Contacts read to load the role list. Sites: only a Customize Agenda page has the setting; Simple shows the default trio.
internal.talk_track: Untick Moderators and Chairpersons under Roles to show and your agenda lists speakers only; feeds follow the same setting.

entries.title: See when each file was uploaded, and by whom
entries.summary: The **Submission files** list view has new **Uploaded** and **Uploaded By** columns. The time is shown in the event's timezone with the zone named. Sort by upload date oldest or newest first, and filter by upload date, to find everything that arrived since you last pulled files. A file's details also say who uploaded it. File request dates now use the event's timezone. Zips built with **Download files bundle...** list `uploaded_at` and `uploaded_by` for every file in **manifest.csv**. Speakers and applicants see when they uploaded each file on their forms.

enable.path: Program → Submissions → Submission files → list view

entries.use_case: A production team pulling decks for the AV crew can see which files came in since their last download and work through them in the order they arrived.

cs_action.note: On for everyone; nothing to turn on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks which files are new since they last downloaded, or keeps their own spreadsheet of what they pulled from Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program and production teams who download session files repeatedly before and during an event.
internal.staff_path: Program → Submissions → Submission files → list view → Uploaded column; sort menu → Upload date + arrow
internal.gotchas: Versioned files show the latest version's upload; earlier versions keep their dates in the session's Files tab history. Custom file fields on contacts and groups have no recorded uploader, so manifest.csv leaves uploaded_by blank for them. Portal forms show the upload time only for files uploaded after this release.

entries.title: Awards: a welcome page before applicants choose a category
entries.summary: Turn on the **Welcome page** in the Awards Form Builder to greet applicants with your program overview, eligibility and guidelines before they choose a category. It supports rich text with no short length limit, a custom button label, and a live preview, and the builder's **Preview** walks through it first. It is off for every existing program.

enable.path: Awards → program → Edit → Form Builder → Welcome page → Show a welcome page before category selection

where.path: Awards Site → Apply → Welcome page (before Select Category)

entries.use_case: Programs with long eligibility rules or guidelines no longer have to squeeze them into the short program description above the category list; applicants read them on their own page first.

cs_action.note: Off by default; existing programs are unchanged.

internal.gotchas: Skipped when an applicant changes the category of an application they already started, and when the page is on but has no title and no message. Not offered on self-serve Awards, whose nomination page has no category picker.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Edit → Form Builder → Welcome page
internal.talk_track: Put your full guidelines on a welcome page that applicants read before they pick a category.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer pastes long instructions into the program description, or asks for an intro page like the one on the Call for Speakers form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers with eligibility rules or detailed guidelines, especially medical and scientific societies.

entries.title: Surveys is on for every event, with a Share panel for links, QR codes and embeds
entries.summary: Attendee **Surveys** no longer needs an Early Access request: every event has **Program → Collect & Review → Surveys**. The new **Share** step gives you the survey link, a print-ready QR code, an embed for your event app or website, and a link and QR code for each session, plus a CSV of every session link to load into Cvent, Swapcard, Grip or your own app. Attendees who open a survey that isn't open yet, has closed or has a bad link now see a plain explanation instead of an error.
entries.use_case: Collect session feedback inside the event app attendees already use: paste the embed, or put each session's own survey link on its session page, and every rating lands on the right session in Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Automatic for every event; nothing to enable. Customers who requested the Surveys beta already have it. Point customers asking for post-event session feedback at the Share step and the CSV of session links.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer runs session evaluations in SurveyMonkey, Cvent or a paper form, or asks how to collect session feedback in their mobile event app.

entries.title: Manage tasks across your whole program with My Tasks, record Task cards and note follow-ups
entries.summary: A new **My Tasks** page (available at the org and event level) lists every task assigned to you or your team, with filters for assignee, event, linked record type, priority and status, sortable columns, bulk **Mark complete** and **Reassign**, and **Export CSV**. A **Tasks** card now appears in the Contact, Session and Sponsor/Exhibitor sidebars so you can create and track tasks directly from any record. On the Notes tab, **Add follow-up** lets you attach a task to any note, with due date, time, assignee and reminder; completed follow-ups show who finished them and offer **Reopen**.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Tasks for your org; then My Tasks appears in the org and event sidebars

where.path: My Tasks (org or event sidebar) · Contact / Session / Sponsor sidebar → Tasks card · Notes tab → Add follow-up

entries.use_case: Event teams juggling dozens of speaker, sponsor and session action items can now see every open task in one place, filter to what is overdue or due today, and mark items complete without leaving the page. Linking a task directly to a contact or session note keeps context together and removes the need for a separate project-management tool.

cs_action.note: The entire Tasks layer is gated to super-users on Platform orgs only. CS must confirm the org is Platform-tier before enabling; self-serve orgs see a 'Tasks are part of Sessionboard Platform' message.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to track speaker or sponsor action items inside Sessionboard, or when they mention using a separate tool like Asana or Trello alongside Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Platform-tier organizers who manage multi-person event teams and need task assignment and follow-up tracking tied to their program records.
internal.staff_path: Requires super-user flag + Platform org/event; access levels read from /user/me/access-levels.
internal.gotchas: Self-serve orgs (Marketing, Learning, Awards workspaces) are blocked at the API level with a 403 TASKS_PLATFORM_ONLY error; the UI surfaces a plain message and renders no card. The web-api PR on branch feature/sb-10486-tasks-layer must also be deployed.
internal.talk_track: Instead of copying contact names into a spreadsheet to track who still needs a bio or headshot, your team can create tasks directly on each contact record, assign them to the right person, set a due date, and see everything overdue in one filtered view — all without leaving Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has /api/guides/tasks covering the API contract, but there is no organizer-facing guide explaining the My Tasks page, the record Tasks card, or note follow-ups; a new guide under /program/tasks or /contacts/tasks should document these surfaces for non-developer users.
draft.why_use_it: Tasks gives your team a single place to create, assign and track action items that are tied directly to the contacts, sessions and sponsors in your program. Each task carries a due date, optional reminder, priority and linked records, so nothing falls through the cracks between email threads and spreadsheets. The My Tasks view lets anyone on the team see their own queue or the full team's workload, filter by status and export for reporting. Follow-up tasks attached to notes keep the reason a task was created visible alongside the conversation that prompted it.

entries.title: Awards: the submission confirmation is sent after payment
entries.summary: On an awards program that charges a fee **on submission**, applicants no longer get the **Submission Confirmation** when they click **Submit** and land on payment. It goes out once, when payment moves the entry from **Pending Payment** to **Submitted** — by card, with a 100% promo code, or through cart checkout. Programs with no fee still send it on submit.

where.path: Awards Site → entry → Complete Your Payment

entries.use_case: Applicants who haven't paid yet are no longer told their entry was received, so nobody assumes they are done while their entry sits unpaid.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Entries that received the early email before this fix were not emailed again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says applicants got a confirmation but their entry shows Pending Payment.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers that charge an entry fee on submission.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Notifications → Submission Confirmation
internal.gotchas: About 30 US entries got the early confirmation before the fix; nothing was resent. Retried payments never send a second email.

entries.title: Sites: applicant buttons and form controls follow the Accent Color
entries.summary: On a Site's applicant pages — apply, cart, checkout, confirmation, request forms and the reviewer home — buttons, radio buttons and checkboxes now use the Site's **Accent Color**, with a text and border shade picked for contrast. **Primary Color** still fills the content boxes, so a white Primary no longer makes the controls invisible.

where.path: Site → apply, cart, checkout, confirmation, request forms, reviewer home

entries.use_case: A Site that uses a white or light Primary Color for clean content boxes keeps visible, on-brand buttons and checkboxes for applicants without any workaround.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Sites with no Accent Color keep their current look. The Primary and Accent hints in the Site builder now describe this.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports invisible or white-on-white buttons, radios or checkboxes on their application form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards and CFP customers whose Site uses a white or very light Primary Color.
internal.staff_path: Site builder → Site → Branding → Signed-in portal
internal.gotchas: Review scoring, My Profile and My Submissions still draw controls from Primary Color; that is a known follow-up.

entries.title: Submission Confirmation: Submitter name names the submitter, and a new Recipient name tag
entries.summary: Participants who get a copy of the **Submission Confirmation** (roles with **Send submission confirmation email** on) were greeted as if they were the submitter. **Submitter name** now always names the person who submitted, and a new **Recipient name** merge tag greets each reader by their own name.
entries.use_case: Moderators and co-presenters copied on a confirmation now read who actually submitted the session, and the email can still address them personally.

cs_action.note: Templates that say 'Dear Submitter name' should switch to Recipient name so each participant is greeted by their own name; Josh updated the 8 US and 1 EU templates found at release.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A speaker or moderator says the confirmation email called them the submitter.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events whose submission forms send the confirmation to participant roles.
internal.staff_path: Submission form → Notifications → Submission Confirmation → Merge tags

entries.title: Review scoring works on phones in Focus mode
entries.summary: On a Site's review page, **Focus** no longer squeezes the scorecard into a sliver on phones and landscape screens. On a phone the submission and the scorecard stack in one scroll; from tablet width the scorecard scrolls in its own pane with **Save review** pinned, so it is always reachable.
entries.use_case: Reviewers can score on their phone between sessions without losing the Save review button.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A reviewer says they can't reach Save review on a phone or tablet.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose reviewers score on mobile devices.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Preview as reviewer, at phone width

entries.title: Reviewers see the Site's welcome message on their home page
entries.summary: The reviewer home on a Site shows the signed-in welcome **Title** and **Description** above the review rounds, as submitters already saw. Sites without a welcome message show nothing extra.
entries.use_case: The welcome text you write for the Site — instructions, deadlines, a thank-you — now reaches your reviewers too.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why reviewers don't see the welcome text on the portal home.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers that run reviews on a Site with a welcome message.
internal.staff_path: Site builder → Portal → Home

entries.title: Review assignments count the right pool for plans that review subsessions
entries.summary: On a review plan's **Assignments** step, **Filtered submissions** now comes from the server on every round, so it matches what **Assign** creates. A plan that reviews subsessions, with none in scope, says *No eligible subsessions match this round's scope and filters* instead of showing a count it could never assign.
entries.use_case: Admins see the real number of submissions a round will assign before they click Assign, so a plan set up for the wrong target is obvious straight away.

cs_action.note: What a plan reviews can't change after creation. A customer whose subsession plan shows 0 needs a new plan that reviews submissions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the assignment count changed or the plan assigns nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using review plans, especially with subsessions.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → plan → Edit → Assignments

entries.title: Reports: pivoted date columns follow your date format
entries.summary: In a side-by-side (pivot) report, renamed date columns such as **Session 1: Starts at** now use the event's export date format in the grid and in CSV and XLSX downloads, like every other date column.
entries.use_case: Pivoted schedules read the same way as the rest of the report, so they can go straight to a printer or a partner.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports raw timestamps in a pivoted report or its export.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who pivot sessions or participants side by side.
internal.staff_path: Reports → a report with Pivot → Download

entries.title: Reports with review fields show only the columns you picked
entries.summary: Adding a review field, such as **Session avg score**, to a report no longer adds about fifteen extra review columns. Reports that read reviews return only the columns the report asks for, in the grid, share links and scheduled reports.

where.path: Reports, report share links and scheduled reports

entries.use_case: Review reports stay clean and match what the admin built, so they can be shared without trimming columns by hand.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Other reports are unchanged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer sees unexpected review columns in a custom report.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers reporting on review scores.
internal.staff_path: Reports → a Sessions report with a review field

entries.title: Automations: checkbox triggers fire on checked or unchecked
entries.summary: When an automation watches a checkbox field, **Changed to a specific value** now offers **Becomes checked** or **Becomes unchecked** instead of a text box, and the automation fires only in that direction. You can't save or enable it with the option on and nothing picked.
entries.use_case: Send an email or assign reviewers the moment a box such as 'Travel booked' or 'Needs AV' is ticked, or when it is cleared.

cs_action.note: Automatic. An automation that typed 'true' before should be reopened and set to Becomes checked.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer's checkbox automation never fires.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using automations on checkbox fields.
internal.staff_path: Automations → automation → When → A field changes → a checkbox field

entries.title: Reviewer import: Tags and Update record if already exists
entries.summary: The reviewer import template has two new columns. **Tags** adds pipe-separated reviewer tags, creating any the event doesn't have. **Update record if already exists** decides what happens to a reviewer already on the event: `TRUE` or blank updates them, `FALSE` skips the row with an error.

where.path: Program → Review → plan → Plan options → Import reviewers

entries.use_case: Committees arrive already tagged by expertise or panel, and an import meant for new people can't overwrite reviewers you have already set up.

cs_action.note: Both columns are optional; old files import exactly as before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer tags reviewers by hand after every import, or asks how to avoid touching existing reviewers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with large review committees.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → plan → Plan options → Import reviewers → Generate Template

entries.title: Call for Reviewers: approve, decline, resend or remove many people at once
entries.summary: The Call for Reviewers people table has row checkboxes and a bulk bar: **Approve**, **Decline**, **Resend invitation** and **Remove**. Each confirms the count first, leaves alone anyone it doesn't apply to, and reports partial failures. It works on events and Awards programs.
entries.use_case: Approve a whole batch of reviewer applications or chase every unanswered invitation in one click instead of row by row.

cs_action.note: Available to anyone who can manage the call.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer has dozens of pending reviewer applications.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events and Awards programs recruiting reviewers through a call.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Call for Reviewers → people table

entries.title: Review progress columns on the Submissions list
entries.summary: **Program → Submissions** has a **Review progress** column group under **Preferences → Columns**: one column per round of every live review plan, reading reviews done out of assigned, such as **3 / 5**.
entries.use_case: Program chairs can see which submissions are still waiting on reviewers without opening each plan.

cs_action.note: On for every event with a review plan. The columns are not in exports and are not sortable yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to see review progress next to their submission fields.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using review plans.
internal.staff_path: Program → Submissions → Preferences → Columns → Review progress
internal.gotchas: Not exported and not sortable yet.

entries.title: Contacts: permissions to create, edit and delete saved views
entries.summary: Event and organization roles have **Can create views**, **Can edit views** and **Can delete views** under **Contacts**, matching Sessions. Without them, the save, rename and delete items are hidden in the Saved Views menu and the API refuses the change. Every existing role has all three.
entries.use_case: Keep shared contact views stable: let coordinators use the team's views without being able to overwrite or delete them.

cs_action.note: Every role was granted all three at release, so nothing changed until an admin turns one off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says someone keeps changing or deleting a shared contact view.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with large event teams sharing contact views.
internal.staff_path: Event → Team → Permissions → role → Contacts
internal.gotchas: Speakers page views live on contacts, so the same switches govern them.

entries.title: Field Rules: a permission to manage rules
entries.summary: A new organization permission, **Can manage field rules**, controls who can open, create, edit and delete Field Rules. Without it the **Field Rules** button is hidden on Library → Fields and the API refuses the request. Every organization role has it on.
entries.use_case: Organizations can let people manage fields without letting them change the rules that rewrite data on every save.

cs_action.note: Granted to every organization role at release.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants to restrict who can change Field Rules.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations using Field Rules.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Team → Permissions → role → Organization Settings → Can manage field rules

entries.title: Bulk Permissions: copy statuses and their role restrictions
entries.summary: **Bulk Permissions** has a new option, **Copy statuses and their role restrictions**. It creates any custom status a target event is missing (never renaming or deleting one) and gives the selected roles the template role's status restrictions, mapped to each event's statuses. The Admin role is skipped and every change is in History.
entries.use_case: Organizations running many events with the same review workflow set up statuses and who may set them once, then roll them out to every event.

cs_action.note: Available to organization admins on Bulk Permissions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer sets up the same custom statuses and status restrictions event by event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with many similar events.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Bulk Permissions

entries.title: Reports and widgets: pick filter values from a list
entries.summary: Filters on option fields — status, track, format, level, tags and custom dropdowns — offer the event's own values in a dropdown (**=**, **!=**, **CONTAINS**) or a multi-select (**IN**, **NOT IN**) in the Report Builder and the dashboard widget builder, instead of a text box. Lists over 1,000 values stay free text.

where.path: Report Builder → Filters; widget builder → Build

entries.use_case: No more typos in filter values: pick the track or status from the list and the report matches exactly.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Saved filters keep their values.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer's report filter returns nothing because a value was typed differently.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone building reports or dashboard widgets.
internal.staff_path: Reports → Report Builder → Filters; Dashboard → Add Widget → Build custom → Build

entries.title: Agenda embed: choose the fields on the session card
entries.summary: An embed's **Agenda** tab has a new switch, **Choose the fields on the session card**. Turn it on and pick the card's own fields — level, speakers, a custom field — and the card shows the title, time and those fields, while the pop-up keeps the Agenda fields. It is off for every existing embed.

enable.path: Publish → Embeds → embed → Field Options → Agenda → Choose the fields on the session card

entries.use_case: Show attendees the details they choose by — level, speakers, a topic — right on the agenda card, without opening every session.

cs_action.note: Off by default; existing embeds render as before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants speakers or a custom field on the agenda card.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who embed their agenda on their own website.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Embeds → embed → Field Options → Agenda

entries.title: Automations: Duplicate and Copy to another event
entries.summary: Each automation's menu has **Duplicate** and **Copy to another event…**. Copies arrive turned off with their own email. Fields, statuses, forms and roles are matched by name in the other event; anything without a match is listed and blocks **Enable** until you fix it and save.
entries.use_case: Build an automation once and reuse it in next year's event, or start a variation from a working copy.

cs_action.note: Available to anyone who can manage automations. Copying automations as part of an event clone ships in a later release.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer rebuilds the same automations for every event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running recurring events.
internal.staff_path: Automations → ⋯ on an automation

entries.title: Interest forms: remove a submission from an event
entries.summary: A submission added to an event can now be taken back: **Remove from event** on the submission's banner unlinks it, keeping the session in the event by default or moving it to the event's trash. The change is audited, and **Add to Event** works again. Deleting the session in the event also clears the link.
entries.use_case: Fix a submission sent to the wrong event, or move it to another, without asking support.

cs_action.note: Moving the session to the trash needs Sessions delete permission in that event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer sees 'This submission cannot be reassigned while it is linked to an event'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Interest Forms across several events.
internal.staff_path: Organization → Interest Forms → form → submission → Remove from event

entries.title: Transcribe: tag voices to any session participant, with roles
entries.summary: On a captured session's transcript page, the **Participants** panel and the speaker-tagging picker list everyone on the session with their role — moderators, chairs, panelists and custom roles, not only speakers.
entries.use_case: A moderator's questions and a chair's introduction are credited to the right person in transcripts, recaps and quotes.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer can't find a moderator to tag in a transcript.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Transcribe on panels and moderated sessions.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → session → Participants

entries.title: Submission forms: hide the character counter on a text question
entries.summary: **Customize question** on a short or long text question has a **Show character count** switch. Turn it off and submitters no longer see a counter such as *3/255*; the limit still applies and *Limit of N characters reached* shows when they reach it.

enable.path: Submission form → question ⋯ → Customize question → Show character count

entries.use_case: Keep forms calm for questions like a name or a title, where a counter adds noise, without giving up the length limit.

cs_action.note: On by default; existing forms are unchanged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to hide the 3/255 counter on a form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with submission forms.
internal.staff_path: Submission form → question ⋯ → Customize question → Show character count

entries.title: Participant Feedback settings say participant, not speaker
entries.summary: The Participant Feedback settings and preview now say *participant* — **What participants see**, **Preview as participant** — because feedback reaches everyone on a session, in any role.
entries.use_case: The wording matches who actually sees the feedback, so admins aren't left wondering whether moderators and chairs are included.

cs_action.note: Copy change only.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks whether chairs or moderators see session feedback.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Participant Feedback.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Participant portal → Participant Feedback

entries.title: Exhibitors & Sponsors settings show what needs Sponsor Pro or Exhibitor Pro
entries.summary: On an event without **Sponsor Pro** or **Exhibitor Pro**, **Event Details → Exhibitors & Sponsors** lists what is included and what needs Pro, with **Ask your account team**. **Add portal** explains why the **Groups** type is locked.

where.path: Event Details → Exhibitors & Sponsors; Add portal

entries.use_case: Admins see why a Groups portal is unavailable and what Pro adds, instead of a locked option with no explanation.

cs_action.note: The note's button sends customers to their account team; be ready to talk about Sponsor Pro / Exhibitor Pro.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why the Groups portal type is greyed out.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events managing sponsors or exhibitors without Pro.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Event Details → Exhibitors & Sponsors; Portals → Create Portal

entries.title: A submission's upload extension now has an end date
entries.summary: Turning on **Accept uploads after the deadline** for one submission now asks for a **New upload due date** in the event's timezone. Its participants can upload until then — in every slot and the poster builder — and uploads close after. Extensions turned on before keep no end date until you set one.
entries.use_case: Give one late speaker until Friday without leaving their uploads open forever.

cs_action.note: Existing extensions (54 in US at release) stay open with no end date until someone sets one.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer grants a late speaker more time to upload.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers collecting files through the portal.
internal.staff_path: Session → Files → Portal uploads → Accept uploads after the deadline

entries.title: Weekly portal summary mentions open file uploads
entries.summary: When a participant's portal is taking session files, the Monday **weekly portal summary** adds a **File uploads** block with the event's due date, or each open upload slot their role owes with its own date. It never sends the email on its own.
entries.use_case: Speakers are reminded where and by when to upload in the email they already get every week.

cs_action.note: Automatic; shown only while uploads are open for that person.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks whether the digest reminds speakers about uploads.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers collecting files through the portal.
internal.staff_path: Settings → Email Templates → System → Weekly Digest Email

entries.title: SSO: enforce login before a sign-in test
entries.summary: **Enforce Login Via SSO** can be turned on for a SAML or OIDC configuration at any stage, not only after a successful sign-in test. Organizations whose security policy rules out sharing test credentials can now enforce SSO.

enable.path: Organization Settings → SSO → SAML or OIDC configuration → Enforce Login Via SSO

entries.use_case: Customers whose IT team can't hand over test credentials (MFA, company-wide SSO) can still require SSO for their domain.

cs_action.note: Enforcing an untested configuration that is wrong stops everyone on that domain from signing in with a password until enforcement is turned off. Make sure an admin outside the domain can turn it off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is stuck on the enforcement step because they can't complete the sign-in test.
internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise customers with strict identity-provider policies.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → SSO → configuration → Enforce Login Via SSO

entries.title: ASP: send the Session ID as Client Session ID
entries.summary: The ASP integration's **Event Settings** has **Use Session ID as Client Session ID**. With it on, a session with no **Client Session ID** of its own is sent to ASP with its Session ID (such as `SESS-123`) as the ContentCode, so it syncs instead of being skipped. Sessions that already have a Client Session ID keep it.

enable.path: Apps → ASP → Event Settings → Use Session ID as Client Session ID

entries.use_case: Customers who don't keep their own Client Session IDs can sync to ASP without inventing codes or copying fields with a rule.

cs_action.note: Opt-in per mapped event. Nothing is written to the session in Sessionboard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An ASP sync skips sessions with 'Client Session ID is missing', or a customer asks to copy the Session ID into Client Session ID.
internal.who_should_get_it: ASP Events customers.
internal.staff_path: Apps → ASP → Event Settings

entries.title: Embeds: Roles to show loads for embed-only editors
entries.summary: The **Roles to show** list on embeds, feeds and Site program views now loads for team members who can manage embeds but don't have Session Settings or Contacts access. They saw an empty list before.
entries.use_case: A web team member who only manages embeds can choose which participant roles the public agenda shows.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An embed editor says Roles to show is empty.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers whose embed editors have restricted roles.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Embeds → embed → Style Options → Participant Roles

entries.title: Apps: a sync log with the vendor's response, and Retry for one record
entries.summary: Each saved connection of an app that writes from Sessionboard — HubSpot, Salesforce, Nimble, iMIS and others — has a **Sync log** listing every write attempt with its result, reason, remote id and the vendor's **Response**. **Retry** re-sends one failed record without running a full sync.
entries.use_case: When a CRM or AMS rejects a record, admins can read exactly why and send just that record again, without re-pushing every unposted order or payment.

cs_action.note: Automatic for connectors that write from Sessionboard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer's CRM or AMS write failed and they want to know why or try again.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with CRM or AMS write connectors.
internal.staff_path: Apps → app → Connections → connection → Sync log

entries.title: Review plans offer imported session fields to reviewers
entries.summary: **Visible Submission Fields to Reviewers** (and the round's filter and card pickers) now also offers custom session fields that hold a value on a session in the event, such as fields filled by an import that are on no submission form. Fields nobody has filled in stay hidden.

where.path: Review plan → Scorecard and reviewer view

entries.use_case: Data brought in by an import — a slide link, a co-presenter detail — can be shown to reviewers without adding the field to a form.

cs_action.note: Automatic. The public ballot's default fields are unchanged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer can't find an imported field in Visible submission fields.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events that import session data and review it.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → plan → Edit → Scorecard and reviewer view

entries.title: Slides: sponsor logos on title slides
entries.summary: The title-slide designer has a **Sponsor logos** section: turn it on, pick the position, logo size and a label such as *Sponsored by*, and each generated slide shows its own session's sponsors in the session's order. Sessions without sponsors show nothing there.
entries.use_case: Give sponsors visibility on every session they back, on the slide the room sees before the talk starts.

cs_action.note: Off by default for every template.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants sponsor logos on session title slides.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with session sponsors that generate title slides.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Slides → template → Sponsor logos

entries.title: Sites: Arial and Georgia as Site fonts
entries.summary: Site branding's **Font Family** now offers **Arial** and **Georgia** alongside Google Fonts. Both are system fonts, so the Site uses them without a font download.
entries.use_case: Organizations whose brand guidelines call for Arial or Georgia can match them exactly on their Site.

cs_action.note: Available in Site branding.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for Arial or Georgia on their Site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Sites, especially awards programs.
internal.staff_path: Site builder → Site → Branding → Font Family

entries.title: Learning: turning on Credits adds CPE, CLE and CEU
entries.summary: When you turn on **Credits**, NASBA CPE Credit, CLE Credit and IACET CEU are added to your credit types if you don't have them, and a line confirms Credits is on. Ask can also rename a page in a course and open a course in the builder.
entries.use_case: Companies offering CPE, CLE or CEU hours can award them right after turning Credits on, without setting up credit types first.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A company turns on Credits and doesn't see CPE or CLE.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning customers awarding professional credit.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Credits → Turn on Credits

entries.title: Learning: question import and Draft questions messages in your language
entries.summary: The question-bank **Import** preview and the course builder's **Draft questions** now show problems, notes and errors in the admin's language (English, German, French or Spanish), and a short lesson gets a message that says it needs more content rather than none.
entries.use_case: Admins who work in German, French or Spanish can fix import problems without reading half-translated English.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A non-English admin reports English or half-translated import messages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning customers working in German, French or Spanish.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Courses → Question bank → Import
